decisions.question: C has no class inheritance or interface hierarchy grammar constructs.
decisions.resolution: NOT APPLICABLE: C emits no extends, implements, or overrides relationships.

decisions.question: Function pointers, macro expansion, and preprocessor control flow cannot always be resolved statically.
decisions.resolution: DECLARED LIMITATION: opaque function-pointer targets and macro-expanded semantics are not fabricated as named relationships.

decisions.question: C completeness scope is tied to the pinned tree-sitter-c grammar.
decisions.resolution: The inventory is exhaustive for the current grammar; future grammar drift requires a new inventory review.

decisions.status: RULED + RESIDUAL CLOSED (2026-09-23) - re-pinned to the clean 0/0 floor on both c corpora
decisions.question: M37 #601 Holy C wave residuals (pinned 2026-09-05): sqlite 100% coverage @60/lang = 9 missing / 105 unexplained (242 @200/lang, 1.07%); jq 99.9% @60 = 4 missing / 28 unexplained (0.94%). Nearly all unexplained sit in 4 GENERATED amalgamation files (autosetup/jimsh0.c, ext/wasm/libcmpp.c, ext/jni/src/c/sqlite3-jni.c, sqlite3-wasm.c) whose JIM_EXPORT/CMPP__EXPORT prototypes and SQLITE_WSD macro-qualified struct definitions cannot parse without macro expansion (C-D2); missing = include-guard macro uses (JIM_SIGNAL_H/__JIM__H/...) and vendored dtoa config macros read inside ERROR-recovered preproc regions; real-file residuals are edges where the ANALYZER is correct (fn-pointer table value reads; ERROR-scope desync in jq builtin.c after a 12-line ERROR span at L2055). The glue-name asymmetry (analyzer isGlueFdName vs oracle isBareFdGlueName, F7 identity-antipattern) was closed positionally so glue-fd names (s3jni_config_log) are suppressed on BOTH sides.
decisions.resolution: RECORDED RESIDUAL: not fixable without macro expansion / whole-file ERROR-span rescoping; the CGD19/CGD33/CGD38 positional artifact rules suppress post-glue variable/type artifacts on BOTH sides. Guarded by: differential baseline floor (sqlite 9/105, jq 4/28 @60/lang - section E validates the jq:c row against this ruling), fixture cgd31-37-regressions pins CGD31-38, regression mutants all caught (251 total incl. 10 c). Any future grammar or corpus change that shifts these numbers regresses the baseline gate. RESIDUAL CLOSED AND THE FLOOR RE-PINNED (2026-09-23): both pinned rows now read 0 missing / 0 unexplained (jq:c sampleSetHash 2b743b65d0eac283, sqlite:c ef6794727cd236d8 in validation/m14/differential-baseline.json), and the M14.0.F5 lane probes through the production entry read the same on both corpora (jq:c 45 files tree-truth 2930/2930 covered 100% MISSING=0 analyzer-edges 2931 unexplained=0 heuristic=0; sqlite:c 60 files 5863/5863 covered 100% MISSING=0 unexplained=0 heuristic=0), so the amalgamation-file class this entry recorded is no longer a live residual. The ruling and the config's floorResidual were updated TOGETHER, which is the gate's own requirement for lowering a documented floor; section E now validates against the clean milestone instead of an allowance. Because the floor got stricter, a future regression of this class FAILS the gate rather than fitting under a stale allowance: the recorded floor no longer describes code that no longer produces it, which is exactly the drift this gate exists to catch. The history above is kept deliberately - the boundary C-D2 declares (no macro expansion, no whole-file ERROR-span rescoping) is still the reason the class existed, and the waves that closed it (#743's grammar rules, #907's declaration-header rule, #912's call-shaped arrival, #920's row-preserving blanking, #921's name-line containment edges) are named in their own records.

decisions.node_type: function-like macro name wrapping a declaration (truth/analyzer disagreement)
decisions.question: The jq c lane's residual after #901: `UNEXPLAINED src/parser.c :: uses yyparse -> YY_INITIAL_VALUE` — a FUNCTION-LIKE macro used to wrap declarations inside yyparse's body (L2229 parent macro_type_specifier, L2230 parent function_declarator). Pre-existing (measured before either #901 edit: MISSING=0 unexplained=1 with the same totals; jq has no forward macro read, so #901's fixes do not touch this lane). A blanket 'function-like macro names are never reads' suppression was attempted and REVERTED — it removed this row and produced MISSING=4 (isleap, YYDPRINTF, decFinish, CFUNC), because the truth counts a macro INVOCATION as BOTH `calls (expr)` and `uses (expr)` and the analyzer's identifier-path uses is the load-bearing match for the second row.
decisions.resolution: REGISTERED as #908 (2026-09-20), with the shape, the four-row lesson as a regression test, and the open adjudication: on the same tree truth derives no row although its CGD13 exemption puts macro names in declaredNames and its use gate should admit the L2229 mention — either its walk misses the mention or a gate excludes it, and one side is wrong. A warning comment now sits at the declaredNames pre-pass so the reverted attempt is not repeated. c's diff column stays red on this single named, reproduced residual. Status at 2026-09-21: still OPEN as #908 — unchanged by the #907 and #910 rounds (the jq c lane's unexplained count is still exactly this one row).

decisions.node_type: swallowed top-level definitions (symbol loss under brace imbalance)
decisions.question: Found by the clang-reference audit of the jq error files (#743's second question): jq src/jv_print.c's public functions `void jv_dumpf`/`void jv_dump` are absent from the catalog entirely (no symbol, no edges) while jv_show/jv_dump_string/jv_dump_string_trunc are present. Mechanism bisected: a brace imbalance (preprocessor-conditional body) makes lines 219-395 parse as ONE function_definition — jv_dump_term's body swallows the rest — and the recovery path that saves nested function_definition nodes does not cover the pair arriving as declaration + compound_statement. The file's first ERROR row is 443, AFTER both definitions, so this is not 'the error region'. F5 cannot see it: a lost symbol produces no lost edge (both sides share the tree).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED (2026-09-21, #907 closed at 13880055): the recovery path now covers the glued arrivals measured on real files — a root-level ERROR holding a bare function_declarator, a pointer-wrapped declarator, a static header, and the decNumber.c arrival shape — and clang's own reference is the acceptance oracle (the audit it drives was corrected in the same round: it counted every FunctionDecl clang attributes to the main file, and because the audit strips `#include <...>` clang relocates libc's implicit prototypes into the stripped file where they carry no location, so 314 claimed losses were 48 real; a definition is now FunctionDecl + CompoundStmt, artifact validation/m12/results/c-clang-def-audit.json). Measured: jq src/jv_print.c lost-defs 2 -> 0 (13 clang defs vs 13 symbols, both targets present); whole-corpus A/B over 434 c files added 23 symbols, every one verified against the source text as a real definition header, 0 non-definition additions and 0 duplicate names; the class-wide jq count 48 -> 39, whose residue (38 flex aliases with no source location and one call-shaped macro-driven site) is named in reviews/m60-907-c-glued-definitions.md and filed as #912. Fixtures c/swallowed-definitions-907, c/swallowed-root-definitions-907, c/swallowed-identifier-arrival-907 + five mutants; c fixtures 12/12, c mutants 27/27, and jq:c canonical 2929/2929 MISSING=0 unexplained=1 (#908).

decisions.node_type: the include ontology (#include as a graph relationship)
decisions.question: M60/#910: c emitted `#include` as a `references` edge carrying metadata.isImport/include_dependency, while typescript/javascript/python/dart/bash/lua/makefile emit the dedicated `imports` kind. Nothing consumed either marker (zero readers outside the analyzers), and the one import-aware reader — the LSP usages file-level section — filters relationship_type IN ('imports','exports') with the root symbol as target, so a c file's dependency list was unanswerable in that surface regardless of how the edge was typed: the include is file -> file with an external specifier, so it has no symbol endpoint on either side. Measured at 4bf9878f: 60-file sample 422 relationships, 0 with a line; 400-file slice 1176 include-ish edges typed `references`.
decisions.resolution: RULED as FIRST-CLASS `imports`, landed c first (2026-09-21) and rolled to the other five languages as their lanes come up. What the ruling means concretely: (1) the analyzer emits the dedicated `imports` kind, target = the path AS WRITTEN (quotes/brackets stripped — the evidence, never a resolved or invented path), line = the path token, metadata keeps relationshipType/isSystemInclude/isImport plus module + fileLevel; (2) the store names the IMPORTER on a file-level row (source_external = the importing file's project-relative path) instead of the file-scope placeholder `global`, so the row can answer 'what does this file include'; (3) brain_import.is_external carries the analyzer's own classification — `<stdio.h>` external, "util.h" internal — where the pool's bare-specifier heuristic (a js/ts idiom) had made both external, and where the store had hardcoded 0 for every language that declares it (c/cpp isSystemInclude, clojure/sql isExternal); (4) the usages response gains an OUTGOING section, fileLevel.dependencies, read by exact importer path, declared separately from the incoming imports/exports rows so 'what this file includes' can never be confused with 'who imports this'. Named limitation: the incoming direction for headers ('who includes this file') is NOT served — the stored specifier is the path as written while the viewed file is a project path, so an exact match is impossible and a basename match would be a guess. Gated by script/m60/verify-910-c-includes.ts on a real index (5 mutants, all caught) plus fixtures c/callsite-lines-825, c/c-completeness, c/macro-composed-include (which now also FORBID the downgraded shape) and mutant c/include-kind-downgraded. Oracle lockstep: the c truth derives the same `imports` label, and the differential's c label allowlist had to admit it — measured 129 MISSING on a 40-file sqlite draw when the oracle changed before the harness allowlist did.

decisions.question: M60/#917 (the residue #916 registered): the vendored families define functions through an export macro standing where the declaration specifier belongs (`CMPP__EXPORT(int, cmpp_stream)( cmpp_input_f inF, … ){ … }`, `S3JniApi(sqlite3_value_text16(),jstring,1value_1text16)(…)`). The published grammar reads the heading as `MACRO(ret, name)` CALLED with `(params)`, so the body is an orphan `compound_statement`, no `function_definition` exists, the definition is not a symbol, its locals publish as FILE-SCOPE names, and every read in its body is attributed to `global`. Counted with the fix's own predicate: 235 headings on sqlite (`ext/jni/src/c/sqlite3-jni.c` 149, `ext/wasm/libcmpp.c` 86), 0 in jq. Two adjudications were needed: is the heading's NAMING occurrence a declaration or a read (it is the defining occurrence, so a declaration), and does truth owe the body a function scope (it does — the oracle's `fnLocals` only runs for `function_definition`, so registering the body's bindings on the analyzer side would suppress a read truth still derives, a MISSING edge created by the fix itself).
decisions.resolution: RULED + FIXED (2026-09-22, #917). One SHAPE RULE, exported by the analyzer (`macroWrappedHeadingShape` / `wrappedBodyAfter`) and imported by the F5 oracle, refusals included (no top-level comma in the macro's argument list ⇒ refused: the separator is the evidence, because a pointer return type puts its type words in a `binary_expression` and leaves one identifier standing; name == macro name and C keywords refused too). The declared name is the macro's LAST identifier argument, and because the C lexer cannot start an identifier with a digit the JNI-mangled spellings arrive split into an `ERROR` holding the leading digits beside the identifier; the join is gated on adjacency and on the ERROR being nothing but a digit-led name fragment. Three call-site gates: `isInsideFunction()` (C has no nested definitions, so an ordinary call chain + block is never a definition), `gluedDefNameOffsets` (the naming occurrence is a declaration — without it the result was ORDER-DEPENDENT: `xTokenize` silent until an earlier heading minted the symbol), and no locals model for the recovered function (mirror of the oracle's `function_definition`-only `fnLocals`). Oracle lockstep was forced by measurement: 67 of the 235 names are also `#define`d in alternative preprocessor branches of the same file, so truth emitted `uses -> cmpp_stream` for the heading that DEFINES `cmpp_stream` (lane MISSING=67) — the mirror is a SKIP on that exact occurrence, never a suppression of the label. Diagnosing it required matching the lane's ENTRY (the analyzer class) to the instrument's (`parseFile`, whose post-processing drops one ERROR-parented mention, `libcmpp.c:9003`). Measured: sqlite:c 315 files `34645/34645 MISSING=0 | 34645 edges unexplained=0 (0%) heuristic=0` from `unexplained=1` — the lane's last unexplained edge (the `BufSize` leak) is gone because the body finally has a Function scope; cpp 28/28/0; jq/fmt/nlohmann byte-identical. Analyzer A/B: 2 files changed, 233 symbols added, 2 removed, 1231 edges removed / 1980 added, REAL-LOSS 0 both ways (1162 re-attributions across 524 pairs, 67 heading-name rows, 2 leaked-local rows). Fixture `c/macro-wrapped-heading-917` (three spellings + controls) proves teeth by revert 14/1 → 15/0; mutant `c/macro-wrapped-heading-loss` caught, c mutants 30/30; F3 c 15/15; F1 all 41 as before; F10 exit 0 (grammar untouched). Registered residue: the POINTER-return spelling (`CMPP__EXPORT(void *, cmpp_mrealloc)(…)`, 6 sites, 1 file, 5 of the 6 names surviving only as their `#define`) is refused by name in the fixture's header and filed as #918.

decisions.node_type: pointer-return macro-wrapped function headings (MACRO(ret*, name)(params){ body })
decisions.question: M60/#918 (the sibling #917's close-out registered by name rather than folding in): the same vendored export macro, but with a POINTER return type (`CMPP__EXPORT(void *, cmpp_mrealloc)(void * p, size_t n){…}`, `CMPP__EXPORT(char const *, cmpp_rc_cstr)(int rc){…}`, `CMPP__EXPORT(cmpp_b *, cmpp_b_borrow)(cmpp *pp){…}`). The parse does NOT orphan the body here — the grammar accepts the heading as a `function_definition` (or, where recovery swallows the region, a `declaration`) whose `type` field is a `macro_type_specifier` holding BOTH macro arguments, the return type inside an ERROR-wrapped `type_descriptor` carrying an `abstract_pointer_declarator` and the NAME as the specifier's LAST named child, with the PARAMETER list in the `declarator` field. The analyzer's declarator route looks for a `function_declarator`, so CGD38's guard drops the node: the definition was never a symbol, its body never a Function scope, and five of the six measured names existed only as the `#define`d macro constant from the file's thunk block. Counted with the fix's own predicate: 6 sites, 1 file (`ext/wasm/libcmpp.c`), 0 in jq.
decisions.resolution: RULED + FIXED (2026-09-22, #918). One shape rule, exported by the analyzer (`macroWrappedTypedHeadingShape`) and shared with the F5 oracle, refusals included. The POINTER is the discriminator and is REQUIRED: `abstract_pointer_declarator` inside the macro's first argument is the parse's own evidence for this spelling, and it is what keeps the VALUE-return headings (the #917 class, whose body is orphaned instead) out of this rule — the reverse is structural too, because a value-return heading's `type` field is never a `macro_type_specifier`. The NAME is read by POSITION (the specifier's last named child, and it must FOLLOW the return-type ERROR), never by node type: for `cmpp_b *` the return type's base is itself a `type_identifier`, so 'the type_identifier that is not the return type' would be a guess. The parameter payload is read structurally: each group's declared name is the RIGHTMOST non-keyword identifier in source order, and a lone identifier is an UNNAMED parameter (`cmpp_b_clear(void)` reports `unknown:void`, never naming the definition after a type word). The DECLARATION spelling is accepted only with all four pieces present (all-identifier ERROR tail, `parenthesized_declarator`, a lone `}` as the declaration's next sibling, no MISSING token but the list's mended `)`), so no span is ever invented. Exactly one asymmetry between the two spellings, and it is a MIRROR: the oracle keys `fnLocals` by `function_definition` startIndex, so the function_definition spelling gets truth-side locals (collected from body declarations) and the declaration spelling gets none — the analyzer registers locals for the first and joins `macroWrappedFunctionNames` (the #917 contract for this) for the second, because registering locals the oracle cannot see fabricates MISSING rows. Measured: A/B over four c corpora — 1 file changed (`ext/wasm/libcmpp.c`), jq/fmt/nlohmann byte-identical; symbols +6/-1 (the single removal is the L219 PROTOTYPE of cmpp_rc_cstr superseded by its definition under the one-symbol-per-name contract); edges +0/-0 at the lane's own pair granularity with 23 re-attributions from `global` to the recovered function; REAL LOSS 0 both ways. Lane: sqlite:c 315 files `34645/34645 (100%) MISSING=0 | 34645 edges unexplained=0 (0%) heuristic=0`, cpp 28/28/0. Fixture c/macro-wrapped-pointer-heading-918 (three pointer spellings, the declaration spelling in the real file's `#ifdef __cplusplus / extern "C" {` context, a value-return CONTROL, an ordinary pointer-returning function + prototype CONTROL, and the unnamed-parameter CONTROL) proves teeth by revert 15/1 -> 16/0; mutant c/macro-wrapped-pointer-heading-loss caught by that fixture alone. NOT claimed: a third sub-shape seen while authoring (the same heading whose body is several statements, leaving the declaration with no glued ERROR tail and the body at file scope) — the census says it occurs in neither c corpus, so the rule refuses it rather than inventing a span.

decisions.node_type: call-shaped declarators: a definition HEADER recovery leaves as a CALL (`static block gen_last_1(void) {`)
decisions.question: M60/#912, part 1 (the residue #907 refused by name). jq src/builtin.c:2067 — `static block gen_last_1(void) {` — was never a symbol. The mechanism is lines 1969-2067 of that file: the replacement text of `#define BINOP(name) CFUNC(f_ ## name, "_" #name, 3),` is itself call-shaped, and a BARE macro name (`BINOPS`) stands as a table entry, so the replacement-text call's argument list desynchronizes recovery and swallows the rest of the table, the table's own `};`, the `#undef` block and the next definition's HEADER — which survives only as an ERROR holding `static`, `block` and a `call_expression gen_last_1(void)`, with the body as a sibling `compound_statement`. The analyzer's `gluedDeclaratorNames` unwrapped `function_declarator` and pointer wrappers only, so this third arrival was invisible; the shape was originally refused in #907 because a macro INVOCATION with a block (`FOREACH(item) {`) presents the identical tree.
decisions.resolution: RULED + FIXED (2026-09-23, #912 part 1). The arrival is admitted on the SAME two evidences the bare-identifier arrival uses (the parameter list must end at the body's `{`; a `#define`'s own logical line is skipped) plus ONE that is this class's own — `declarationSpecifierRunBefore`: a contiguous run of at most three bare `identifier` siblings directly before the call, comments skipped, broken by any other sibling type and by a preprocessor directive's operand, must carry a RESERVED declaration word. That is a different question from the bare arrival's header test (`declarationHeaderPresent`, "any identifier since the previous terminator"), and the difference is MEASURED, not cautious: gating this arrival on the looser header test publishes the 33 `#define osCloseHandle ((BOOL(WINAPI*)(HANDLE))aSyscall[1].pCurrent)` sites of sqlite os_win.c/os_unix.c as functions (+33 symbols, +4 resolved `uses` edges), because the directive's own words supply the "type" token and the next table entry supplies the `{`. The two guards were additionally compared over the whole candidate class the two c corpora can present (434 .c/.h files) and decide every site identically, so the strict one is chosen on the class the comparison cannot see. The recovered symbol carries `glueNameShape: call-declarator` (a third value in the arrival's metadata), is emitted at file scope under the C no-nested-functions invariant, is `private` from the `static` in its own declaration window, and the heading's one pre-existing read — `calls global -> gen_last_1` at the definition line, the call visitor's own contract for any `call_expression`, derived identically by the oracle — is left EXACTLY as it was rather than silently suppressed. Measured: A/B through the production entry, pre-fix vs post-fix, only this file differing — jq (77 files) +1 symbol `2067:function:gen_last_1`, -0 symbols, 0 relationships changed; sqlite (357 files) BYTE-IDENTICAL (24072 symbols / 141448 relationships both sides; dump md5 bb144ff40d1d189c619af8f2f9b9451f on BOTH sides). The A/B was re-run after the shared-predicate refactor, against the FINAL analyzer bytes: the post-jq dump (md5 a930802d61e2759c7d2c03d9268f4ff2) equals the earlier fixed-build dump, so the refactor was output-neutral, and the pre-jq dump re-made at HEAD (md5 f893d0b06721cf7597176eb410648895) reproduced the earlier pre dump byte-for-byte — which is what licenses reading the recorded pre-sqlite dump (same HEAD analyzer bytes f4a87d6d796045d81b89f864c6a01e33, same instrument) as the pre side. At the fixture level the sole symbol difference is the recovered one and all 73 relationships are byte-identical. Lane with the recovery live: `[jq] c: files=45 tree-truth=2930 covered=2930 (100%) MISSING=0 | analyzer-edges=2931 unexplained=0 (0%) heuristic=0`, `[sqlite] c: files=60 tree-truth=6713 covered=6713 (100%) MISSING=0 | analyzer-edges=6713 unexplained=0 (0%) heuristic=0`. Fixture c/call-shaped-declarator-912 (jq's own lines 1969-2067 verbatim; CONTROL A an invocation with a block and no declaration word — refused; CONTROL B the sqlite `#define` replacement-text class — arrive-and-refuse; CONTROL C a clean `static block f(void)` definition, ordinary route, no recovery metadata, not claimed twice; plus a SECOND desync with different names so a rule keyed to the first table's text is visible) proves teeth with the recovery live (c lane 17 pass / 0 fail) and the reverted analyzer (mutant c/call-shaped-declarator-loss) failing exactly this fixture (0 -> 1 failures; the other 31 c mutants stay caught, and the fixture's controls fail if the rule is widened into accepting them). NOT claimed: the second arrival spelling where the swallowed table ends in `};` and the header arrives as a bare identifier — already covered by #907 round 2 and pinned by c/swallowed-identifier-arrival-907. PART 2 of the same issue was RE-CLASSIFIED by measurement rather than recovered, and the issue's premise was wrong: the 38 `jq/src/lexer.c` aliases were called 'structurally unnameable — no source location, written-in-text=false'. Re-measured, ALL 38 are already published, each under the name the file writes. Every one of the 38 names occurs in the file's text exactly once, as the REPLACEMENT of a flex rename directive (`#define yy_create_buffer jq_yy_create_buffer`, itself guarded by `#ifdef yy_create_buffer` so an external declaration can win), and NONE of them is followed by `(` anywhere in the file; the definitions are written under the pre-rename spelling and the analyzer publishes exactly those (38 of 38 pre-rename counterparts present: `yy_create_buffer` 1973, `yy_scan_string` 2218, `yy_scan_bytes` 2231, …). The audit's names are the PREPROCESSOR'S PROJECTION, not the source's — publishing `jq_yy_create_buffer` would publish a name that appears nowhere as a declarator, and the `_ALREADY_DEFINED` guards exist so another declaration can own it. Class: naming projection, not recoverable loss. Independent check re-emitted with the round: clang's own AST over jq's error-file set now reads 738 main-file definitions / 38 lost, and all 38 are exactly these flex aliases (`validation/m12/results/c-clang-def-audit.json`).

decisions.node_type: engine-level: the C/C++ preprocessing blanks a MULTI-LINE `__attribute__((…))` / `__declspec(…)` by REPLACING the match with spaces, which destroys the newline(s) inside it and moves every later row
decisions.question: M60-C/#920 (found by the M59 Tier A oracle on the zig corpus, i.e. by an instrument that does NOT share the analyzer's tree). `src/ast/engine.ts` `parseRaw` blanks compiler extensions before parsing under the comment 'This preserves exact byte bounds and line numbers for Tree-sitter'. The two patterns `__attribute__\s*\(\([\s\S]*?\)\)` and `__declspec\s*\([\s\S]*?\)` are the ONLY ones in that block that can match ACROSS A NEWLINE, and each was replaced with `" ".repeat(match.length)` — byte count preserved, every newline inside the match DESTROYED. Every node after such an attribute therefore landed one (or more) rows too high: `zig/lib/libtsan/tsan_rtl.cpp` line 59's `bool OnFinalize(bool failed);` was reported at row 57 by `ASTEngine.parseTree` while a raw web-tree-sitter parse of the same bytes reports row 58.
decisions.resolution: RULED + FIXED (2026-09-23, #920). The blanker is now `blankKeepingNewlines` (`match.replace(/[^\n]/g, " ")`) for BOTH multi-line patterns, so byte offsets (the safety primitives' comment/string-masking contract) and `startPosition.row` are both preserved; the single-token replacements (`__restrict__`, `__cdecl`, …) cannot span a newline and are untouched. Measured blast radius, with the engine's own regexes over git ls-files (`script/m14/tmp/c912-attr-shift.ts`): zig 14032 C/C++ files, 76 carry a destroyed newline, worst case 138 rows (`lib/libc/wasi/libc-bottom-half/sources/__wasilibc_real.c`), 340 rows destroyed in total; the four pinned c/cpp corpora contain ONE such file (`fmt/test/gtest/gtest/gtest.h`). Effect on the oracle that found it (M59, c/cpp scoped, 120 files/lang): cpp INCONSISTENT 682 -> 65, c unchanged at 101 (c's residue is the SEPARATE contains-on-a-later-name class below); on the canonical 40-file draw: cpp 41 -> 37 and +5 relationships (the shift had merged/split rows in the one affected file), c 0 -> 0. A/B with a deterministic instrument over fmt (the lane's own F5 sample ROTATES by design — cold-pool, #760 — so lane numbers are not comparable across runs; `script/m14/tmp/c920-ab.ts` uses `git ls-files` order): 1 file changed, the pair multiset of symbols and relationships IDENTICAL (0 names lost, 0 gained), 2782 rows moved +1, 42 unchanged; jq's c and cpp lanes are byte-identical (hash `2b743b65d0eac283` / `94decf48201d1620` both sides) because that corpus has no multi-line attribute. NOT visible to any existing gate: the M14 fixture runner parses the fixture text itself and calls `analyzer.analyze` directly (only vue/svelte go through `parseFile`), so the engine's blanking never runs in the fixture lane; and the F5 differential cannot see it by construction (oracle and analyzer share the tree). Therefore a gate was added where the contract lives, registered as `M14.0.F12` (evidence `validation/m14/results/M14.0.F12.json`, claim level L3, layers engine/analyzer/corpus): `script/m14/verify-attr-line-base-920.ts` (`bun run audit:attr-line-base`, wired into `npm run verify` after `audit:grammar`) compares `ASTEngine.parseTree` against a raw parse of the same bytes keyed by BYTE OFFSET (node types may legitimately differ — blanking removes attributes from the grammar's view — which is why type is never the key), asserts the blanked text keeps the input's byte length, and SELF-TESTS that the same comparison catches the pre-fix blanker (13/13 sample files, so the check can fail). Fixture `cpp/multiline-attribute-line-base-920` pins the analyzer's own line choices on a file carrying the shape (and that `contains` takes the child's line); its rationale states that the fixture lane does NOT exercise the engine path, so the two instruments are never confused.

decisions.node_type: contains edges onto a child whose NAME is written on a later line than the child's declaration start (`void NORETURN\nCheckFailed(…)`, `typedef enum { … } morder;`, `typedef CombinedAllocator<…>\n    InternalAllocator;`, `struct { … } options;`)
decisions.status: RULED + FIXED (2026-09-23, #921) - the containment edge takes the NAME line; the symbol range is unchanged
decisions.question: The M59 Tier A residue that REMAINS after C-D9's fix, measured on the same 120-file c/cpp sample: 101 c + 65 cpp landed relationships whose claimed line does not contain the name they claim, and every one is a `contains` edge. The shape is always the same: the child symbol's `range.startLine` is the start of its declaration NODE (the `void`, the `struct`/`union`/`enum`/`typedef` keyword, the `struct {` of an anonymous aggregate), while the name the edge claims is written on a later line. Both analyzers set `line_number: s.range?.startLine` for `contains` deliberately, with the comment that the edge 'moves WITH its symbol — the child's own declaration line, so the edge and the symbol range can never disagree (the JVM lesson)'.
decisions.resolution: REGISTERED, not yet fixed, because the two readings are different CONTRACTS and the repository already pins one of them for other edge types: `cpp/callsite-lines-825` and the M59 oracle require a relationship's line to be the line of the node that NAMES it — for the analyzer's own `references`/`calls`/`extends` edges this is implemented (`nameLine` prefers the grammar's `name` field), and the c-level fixture forbids the wrapped `struct` keyword's line for exactly this reason — while the symbol's `range.startLine` is deliberately the declaration node's start (fixture `c/callsite-lines-825`: symbol `seed` is pinned at the `struct` keyword's line 31 while `references seed -> Tally` is pinned at the name's line 32). So either the `contains` edge's line must follow the NAME (matching every other relationship type, and the independent oracle), or the child symbol's range must be narrowed to the name line (making the edge and the range agree, which is what the current comment optimises for) — and the second option moves symbol ranges, which other consumers (search, edit anchors, the M73 line base) read. Measured so it can be decided on numbers rather than taste: 166 rows on the M59 c/cpp 120-file draw (101 c, 65 cpp), 37 on the canonical 40-file draw (cpp only; c 0 there). Filed as **#921** (labels `lang:c`, `lang:cpp`) so the M60 matrix's tracker cell keeps reading the residue instead of a document. Nothing is published today that a consumer would read as wrong by more than one line, and no name is lost — the edges and symbols are all present and correctly attributed; only the `line_number` on `contains` disagreed with the oracle's name-on-line rule. RULED + FIXED (2026-09-23, #921): the edge now carries the line that NAMES the child — the rule every other relationship type already follows (nameLine prefers the grammar's name field) and the rule the M59 oracle checks — while the symbol's range stays the whole declaration node, because search, edit anchors and the M73 line base read it. The name's own line is recorded where the name node is in hand (metadata.nameLine, on the symbol kinds that can own a containment edge; the emission falls back to range.startLine exactly as before when it is absent). Measured: the M59 Tier A oracle on the same pinned 120-file c/cpp draw reads 166 INCONSISTENT -> 0 (c 101 -> 0, cpp 65 -> 0; consistent 13,978 -> 14,079 and 24,083 -> 24,148; noLine 0 in both lanes, so the #825 contract is intact), and the model-level A/B over the four pinned corpora (jq 79 + sqlite 120 + fmt 74 + nlohmann-json 120 = 393 files, production entry, before = the analyzers at HEAD trap-restored and md5-checked) reads 0 symbol differences, 0 relationship identity or count changes, 42 contains rows moved, 0 rows of any other type moved, 9,583 contains rows unchanged — lines only, and only on the relationship kind this entry is about. Fixtures c/contains-name-line-921 and cpp/contains-name-line-921; mutant cpp/contains-line-at-declaration-start (a result-level reproduction of the pre-fix output) CAUGHT by the cpp fixture alone (cpp mutants 22/22, c mutants 32/32, no survivors). TWO MEASURED CORRECTIONS, recorded rather than smoothed. (1) The issue's own 101-c split is the ORACLE's lane, not the analyzer's: every one of those rows is in a .h file that this repository's language-detection policy dispatches to cpp (verified per file — the row comes back from parseFile with the cpp language), so the c analyzer's own residue was 0, and its fixture pins the invariant instead (its member extractor ranges a field at its DECLARATOR — rawDecl skips the type specifiers — so its declared-name line and its range start already coincide). For the same reason there is deliberately NO c twin mutant: it would SURVIVE on any c fixture and prove nothing, which is the measurement that retired cpp/metadata-only-line-second-base. (2) The round SAW two owner-attribution anomalies and did not fold them in, both pre-existing and both invisible to the oracle after this fix: NORETURN contains CheckFailed (zig/lib/libtsan/sanitizer_common/sanitizer_common.h — a namespace-scope function published as a method of a MACRO name that is not itself a symbol) and members of different anonymous aggregates in one file all owned by the synthesised name anonymous (sanitizer_platform_limits_netbsd.cpp). Neither is a line defect, and the oracle cannot see them because it checks the child's name on the line, which is now right.

decisions.node_type: the pinned grammar's parse-success floor on the c corpora - how much of each corpus tree-sitter-c can actually parse (#743, CONV-CPPC-1), and the gate that keeps the number honest
decisions.status: RULED + RECORDED (2026-09-23) - the floors are measured and pinned, the gate that watches them is in the battery with a self-test that can fail, and the grammar-wave remainder is refused on measurement (F11)
decisions.question: F5 compares the analyzer against the oracle and BOTH walk the same partial tree, so a grammar that cannot represent a region produces two equal sides: parity measures agreement, not coverage. Recovery keeps symbols flowing through an ERROR region, which is what makes the gap silent - a 60% error rate and a 0% error rate can both read 'no symbol loss'. So what may a consumer of the c lane assume about grammar coverage, and what watches it?
decisions.resolution: MEASURED, PINNED AND WATCHED. The floors (validation/m14/parse-success-baseline.json; the per-run artifact is validation/m14/results/M14.0.F10.json): sqlite:c 346 files, 200 carry an ERROR node or a MISSING token (57.8%; ERROR 52.6% / MISSING 36.1%; damaged lines median 3, max 429); jq:c 76 files, 26 (34.2%; ERROR 25.0% / MISSING 22.4%; median 4, max 61). #743's own census read 44.4% on jq when it was filed, and the grammar waves landed since (#743b's __has_include, #743c's leaf gate, #907's declaration-header rule, #912's call-shaped arrival, #920's row-preserving blanking) are why the floor is re-pinned rather than quoted. THE GATE IS NOW IN THE BATTERY: script/m14/verify-parse-success.ts (M14.0.F10) existed but was wired into no chain - a gate nobody runs - and now runs inside `npm run verify` immediately after the F1 grammar audit, with `audit:parse-success-selftest` ahead of it. THE SELF-TEST IS WHY IT CAN BE TRUSTED: it measures one REAL lane and drives the gate's own verdictFor/exitCodeFor through every branch it claims - floor equal to the measurement (pass), floor above (pass-improved), floor below (FAIL), a floor pinned at 0% with any damage (FAIL, the hard rule #743 asks for), a CLEAN lane against a 0% floor (pass, the false-positive direction), a moved sample (sample-moved, which is NOT a pass), a lane absent from the baseline (unpinned), the same lane under --update-baseline (pinned), and the exit mapping fail-1 / needs-repin-2 / pass-0. Mutations proved the self-test can fail: folding sample-moved into pass is caught naming that branch (exit 1) and deleting the regression direction is caught naming both FAIL branches (exit 1), each restored byte-identical afterwards. The self-test also REFUSES a lane with no damaged file rather than passing vacuously, because such a lane cannot exercise the FAIL direction at all. NOT CLAIMED HERE: the grammar long tail is not fixed. The candidates censused for it are refused on measurement by M14.0.F11 (script/m14/verify-grammar-leaves.ts), whose G3 output gate reads real losses (21 vanished symbols and 52 lost pairs for the tree-preserving cpp candidate) while G1 and G2 pass, so the remaining damage is a PINNED RESIDUAL that a live gate keeps visible. No consumer of the c lane may read 'MISSING=0' as 'the grammar parses everything'; the floors above are the honest number.
